why: Second owner-curated EaseUI kinetic sample. Paired with the hyper-gloss row on purpose: same author, same set, different aesthetic, so a rule that fires on both is reading the house style rather than the page. Self-contained. Origin: EaseUI/app/public/samples/kinetic/01-abyssal-void-tech.html, copied 2026-08-30, parity verified.
reviewNote: Owner-authored. The three copy-tell rows (theater-slop, marketing-buzzword) are taste calls on his own words — worth his eye even though I ruled them tp.

verdicts.reason: Same root cause as the hyper-gloss row, and measured the same way: the <title> is a multi-line leaked prompt dump, not the document's text aggregated into one fact. Head metadata carries role:"body" out of html-extractor's emitText and is therefore judged as prose. Two independent pages producing the identical shape is what makes this a rule-input defect rather than a page defect. Fixed at the extractor with a "metadata" TextRole.
verdicts.message: 1 body run(s) over 400 characters with no container constraint visible to this tier

verdicts.reason: Inter again, on a second sample with a completely different look. That is the finding: the aesthetic changes and the typeface does not, so the face is carrying none of it.
verdicts.message: Inter is on so many surfaces it no longer carries personality

verdicts.reason: Line 378 is `radial-gradient(circle at center, transparent 0%, #050505 80%)` — a centred vignette behind the hero, ambient depth with no light source. The rule's exact target, present as described.
verdicts.message: 1 radial gradient(s) used as ambient depth

verdicts.reason: "stunning" in the hero paragraph promises the reader a feeling instead of saying what the thing does. A taste call rather than arithmetic, so flagged for owner review — but the rule is reading the word correctly.
verdicts.message: theatrical intensifier(s): "stunning" — promises a feeling instead of describing the thing

verdicts.reason: Line 490 reads "Next-generation primitives built for the modern web stack." — a sentence that survives having its subject swapped for any other product. Textbook for this rule.
verdicts.message: 1 generic SaaS phrase(s): "next-generation" — say what the product literally does
